name: Reddy Brown
lede: Reddy Brown is a modifier name: "reddy," an informal variant of "reddish," attached to the parent color [[brown]].

sections.title: A modifier on brown
sections.body:
The name follows one of the library's most common patterns: the modifier "reddy" (an informal spelling of "reddish") placed in front of the parent color, [[brown]] [1]. This exact label is first recorded in 2010, in the xkcd color survey, a large, informal internet survey in which hundreds of thousands of visitors typed their own name for a swatch; the library keeps names that enough people typed the same way [1][2]. No source consulted here records any coiner beyond that crowd, so the name's inventor is undocumented [1]. The hex #6E1005 is a screen approximation of a very dark, red-leaning brown, close to a dried-blood shade [1].

Its nearest library look-alike is [[blood-red]], about 2.9 units away in LCH space, read as almost the same color [1].

Further along the same family are [[maroon]], more vivid, and [[rosewood]], almost the same color [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In the ColorHub painting archive this hue appears in 353 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.5 percent, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1460s (8 of 71 paintings from that decade), and Amedeo Modigliani, Juan Correa de Vivar and Sandro Botticelli use it most often relative to their output [3]. These are computed color matches on varnished, photographed canvases, not pigment identifications [3].
